corrections.new:
The verification products are distinct nominal types. The API provides no conversion, `Deref`,
or field projection from a weaker verification product to a stronger one; projections from
stronger products to weaker products are permitted.
corrections.old:
The products the verifier operations return are distinct types whose representations are
private to their own modules, so a product that establishes a weaker proposition cannot be
passed where a stronger one is required: a floor-verified request is not a full-profile
verified request, a bound response is not an unbound one, and a delegated response is not a
trust-seam one.
corrections.reason: THM-0047, in this theorem's dependency closure, fields statement and scope, replaced by the owner's Ruling 16.1 text. The old statement said the products' representations are private to their own modules; every field of the two request products is pub, so it was false. The new statement claims what the code establishes: distinct nominal types with no API conversion, Deref or field projection from a weaker product to a stronger one, stronger-to-weaker projections permitted. The new scope states that request products can be assembled by hand and that possession provenance is THM-0051's.

corrections.new:
This is a one-way nominal-separation claim, not an unconstructibility claim. The request
products `CryptographicFloorVerifiedRequest` and `VerifiedMcpRequest` retain public fields, so
values can be assembled by hand. Possession provenance is addressed separately by THM-0051.
corrections.old:
Type separation only. It does not establish that the value a consumer holds was produced by
the operation whose type it has for THAT consumer's exchange — possession provenance is a
proposition about the caller and is registered against the serving composition. It
establishes nothing about what any of the operations verify.
